---
title: "Championships: NBA and WNBA eras"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Takeaways
- **NBA playoffs punish threes and rim attempts.** Points per three-point attempt fell in the playoffs in all
  23 seasons (−0.040 points per shot). Rim attempts fell in 87% of seasons. Mid-range shots held up best.
- **WNBA playoffs show no reliable shot-zone penalty.** Every zone's 95% interval includes zero; with 8-12
  playoff teams a year the sample is small.
- **The WNBA is about six years behind the NBA on the three-point shift, and the gap has grown.** In 2026,
  37% of WNBA shots were threes, about where the NBA was in 2019-20. In 2017-2020 the gap was about three years.
- **Recent WNBA champions are ahead of their own league.** From 2022 to 2026 they took 5 percentage points more of
  their shots from three, and 7.5 points fewer at the rim, than the league average. NBA champions have stayed within 3 points of their league.
:::

Everything on this page is association, not causation, and each league is measured against itself.

## Which shots survive the playoffs?

Points per shot in the playoffs minus the regular season, by zone. Below zero = the shot got worse in the
playoffs. Each league is shown on its own.

```{python}
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from _viz import md
from _viz import show, read, SERIES, end_labels
z = read("step5_playoff_zone_by_season.csv")
zones = ["three", "rim", "paint / short mid", "long mid"]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("NBA", "WNBA"), shared_yaxes=True, horizontal_spacing=0.08)
for j, lg in enumerate(["NBA", "WNBA"], 1):
    for zone, col in zip(zones, SERIES):
        d = z[(z.league == lg) & (z.zone == zone)].sort_values("season")
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.season, y=d.pps_change, name=zone, legendgroup=zone, showlegend=(j == 1),
                        mode="lines+markers", line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=6, color=col),
                        hovertemplate=f"{lg} {zone}: " + "%{y:+.3f}<extra></extra>", row=1, col=j)
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1), row=1, col=j)
fig.update_layout(height=420, yaxis_title="playoff minus regular-season pts/shot", legend=dict(y=1.14))
show(fig)
```

```{python}
r = read("step5_playoff_zone_resilience.csv").dropna(subset=["pps_change"])
r["95% interval"] = [f"{lo:+.3f} to {hi:+.3f}" for lo, hi in zip(r.lo95, r.hi95)]
r["seasons worse in playoffs"] = r.seasons_worse_in_playoffs.map(lambda x: f"{x:.0%}")
r["avg change"] = r.pps_change.map(lambda x: f"{x:+.3f}")
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + r[r.league == lg][["zone", "seasons", "avg change", "95% interval", "seasons worse in playoffs"]].to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Which era is each league in?

How each league chooses its shots in the regular season: share of field-goal attempts from three, and from the
mid-range.

```{python}
from _viz import LEAGUE
p = read("step5_league_profiles.csv")
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("Share of shots from three", "Share of shots from mid-range"),
                    horizontal_spacing=0.1)
for j, f in enumerate(["three_share", "mid_share"], 1):
    for lg, col in LEAGUE.items():
        d = p[p.league == lg]
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.season, y=d[f], name=lg, legendgroup=lg, showlegend=(j == 1), mode="lines+markers",
                        line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=6, color=col),
                        hovertemplate=f"{lg}: " + "%{y:.1%}<extra></extra>", row=1, col=j)
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".0%")
fig.update_layout(height=380, legend=dict(y=1.16))
show(fig)
```

**How many years behind the NBA is the WNBA?** For each WNBA season, the NBA season with the same share
(NBA series smoothed over 3 seasons). Blank where the WNBA value is outside the NBA's range.

```{python}
y = read("step5_wnba_years_behind.csv")
fig = go.Figure()
for f, nm, col in [("three_share", "three-point share", "#2a78d6"), ("mid_share", "mid-range share", "#eb6834")]:
    d = y[y.feature == f]
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.wnba_season, y=d.years_behind, name=nm, mode="lines+markers",
                    line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=8, color=col),
                    hovertemplate=nm + ": %{y:.1f} years behind<extra></extra>")
fig.update_layout(height=340, yaxis_title="years behind the NBA", xaxis_title="WNBA season", legend=dict(y=1.12))
show(fig)
```

## How champions differ from their own league

Champion's share of shots minus its league's share that season, averaged by era (percentage points).
Positive = the champion took more of that shot than the league did.

```{python}
c = read("step5_champion_vs_league.csv")
import pandas as pd
c["era"] = pd.cut(c.season, [2003, 2010, 2016, 2021, 2026], labels=["2004-10", "2011-16", "2017-21", "2022-26"])
cols = {"three_share_vs_league": "threes", "rim_share_vs_league": "rim", "mid_share_vs_league": "mid-range",
        "assisted_share_vs_league": "assisted makes"}
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    g = c[c.league == lg].groupby("era", observed=True)
    t = (g[list(cols)].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=cols)
    t.insert(0, "champions", g.size())
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + t.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Champion identity: offense, defense, and archetype mix

Each champion's offense and defense relative to its own league (points per 100 possessions; up and right = better).
*Offense-led* or *defense-led* when one side's edge beats the other's by 3 or more points; otherwise *balanced*.

```{python}
ci = read("step5_champion_identity.csv")
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("NBA champions", "WNBA champions"), horizontal_spacing=0.1)
for j, (lg, col) in enumerate(LEAGUE.items(), 1):
    d = ci[ci.league == lg]
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.off_edge, y=d.def_edge, mode="markers", name=lg, showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=10, color=col, line=dict(width=2, color="#fcfcfb")),
                    customdata=d[["season", "team", "off_rank", "def_rank", "n_teams", "identity"]],
                    hovertemplate="%{customdata[0]} %{customdata[1]}<br>offense #%{customdata[2]:.0f}, defense #%{customdata[3]:.0f} of %{customdata[4]}<br>%{customdata[5]}<extra></extra>",
                    row=1, col=j)
    for _, r in d[d.season >= 2022].iterrows():
        fig.add_annotation(x=r.off_edge, y=r.def_edge, text=f"{r.team} {r.season % 100:02d}", showarrow=False,
                           yshift=13, font=dict(size=11), row=1, col=j)
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1), row=1, col=j)
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1), row=1, col=j)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="offense edge vs league"); fig.update_yaxes(title_text="defense edge vs league", col=1)
fig.update_layout(height=420, hovermode="closest")
show(fig)
```

Champions' archetype minutes share minus the league average, by era (percentage points).

```{python}
ci["era"] = pd.cut(ci.season, [2003, 2010, 2016, 2021, 2026], labels=["2004-10", "2011-16", "2017-21", "2022-26"])
arch = [c for c in ci.columns if c.startswith("arch_vs_league::")]
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    g = ci[ci.league == lg].groupby("era", observed=True)
    t = (g[arch].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=lambda c: c.split("::")[1])
    t.insert(0, "identity mix", g.identity.agg(lambda s: ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in s.value_counts().items())))
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + t.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Champion ingredients by era

Share of champions with each loosely defined ingredient. They're meant to show drift, not to be a recipe.

```{python}
e = read("step5_champions_by_era.csv")
cols = {"C1_primary_scorer": "primary scorer", "C2_secondary_scorer": "secondary scorer", "C3_spacing_big": "spacing big",
        "C4_perimeter_d": "perimeter defender", "n_high_usage": "high-usage players"}
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + e[e.league == lg][["era", *cols]].rename(columns=cols).round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Does roster mix predict titles better than team strength?

Forward-chained test: train on past seasons, predict the next champion. Higher log-likelihood is better.
So far roster mix does not beat net rating alone in either league.

```{python}
t = read("step5_B_title_cv.csv")
t = t[["league", "model", "test_seasons", "mean_loglik_champion", "uniform_baseline_loglik", "mean_prob_on_champion"]]
t.columns = ["league", "model", "test seasons", "log-lik (champion)", "log-lik (random pick)", "avg prob. on champion"]
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + t[t.league == lg].drop(columns="league").round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Can roster composition alone pick champions?

The same forward-chained test with **no net rating, win % or team ratings**: only archetype mix, player
efficiency, stars, age, defensive stats, and which players were available for the playoffs.

```{python}
nn = read("step5_title_no_net_cv.csv")
nn = nn[["league", "model", "mean_prob_on_champion", "champion_ranked_1st", "champion_in_top3"]]
nn.columns = ["league", "model", "avg prob. on champion", "champion ranked 1st", "champion in top 3"]
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + nn[nn.league == lg].drop(columns="league").round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

Roster-only models beat a random pick but not net rating yet. The strongest one counts only players available
for the playoffs.
